framing.stringency: This is the scTab validation blood subset: 8483 cells x 19331 genes, standard scTab feature space, not pre-normalized, drawn from 25 batches. No explicit median-genes-per-cell or mito-fraction summary is attached, so the decision rests on the fact that this is a moderate-sized, curated benchmark subset (not deep, not razor-thin) rather than on a visibly bad quality signal. Weigh whether 8483 cells give enough margin to discard some for safety, or whether the curated nature of scTab data argues for keeping most cells intact.
framing.flag_doublets: This blood subset has 8483 cells spread across 25 batches, averaging roughly 340 cells per batch. Decide whether this per-batch loading density is high enough that doublet detection would meaningfully catch loading-rate artifacts, versus being too sparse per batch for doublet calls to be worthwhile.

framing.method: This blood-tissue subset has 8305 cells x 15290 genes (scTab feature space, gene names attached post-hoc), median 3289 UMI counts and 1181 detected genes per cell, and no doublet flag was applied. Depth is moderate rather than shallow, but the data span 25 distinct batches, which is a lot of potential composition/library-size heterogeneity to reconcile before clustering or DE. Choose the normalization based on how much you trust a fixed global scaling versus a data-driven size factor, and whether the 15290-gene matrix is shallow enough to need variance-stabilizing residuals.

framing.n_hvg: This is peripheral blood data (8,305 cells, 25 batches) already restricted to the ~15,290-gene scTab feature space, with scran-pooling normalization applied. Blood typically contains a mix of abundant lymphoid/myeloid populations plus rarer subsets (e.g., basophils, pDCs, plasmablasts) that could be diluted in a small HVG set. The choice of how many highly variable genes to select from the 15,290 available genes determines whether rare blood subtypes are captured or whether the signal is concentrated on the dominant, high-count cell types.
framing.n_pcs: With 8,305 cells, 25 batches, and normalized expression from scran pooling, the number of principal components retained determines how much fine-grained structure (e.g., subtle blood subtype differences) versus batch/technical noise is carried into downstream steps. Given the moderate cell count and batch diversity, this decision turns on how much of the variance beyond the dominant axes reflects real biological structure versus batch-driven noise.

framing.integrate: This blood-tissue subset has 8305 cells split across 25 batches (an average of ~332 cells per batch), with 15290 genes in the scTab feature space and normalization already done via scran pooling. Decide whether these 25 batches represent distinct samples/donors likely to produce technical separation in the 50-PC embedding (which currently explains only 24.9% of variance), rather than being replicates of the same condition that should mix naturally.
framing.method: If integration is needed, choose a method suited to correcting 25 batches over 8305 cells in the 50-PC embedding (variance explained 0.249) built from 2000 HVGs.

framing.resolution: This is a blood sample with 8305 cells pooled from 25 donors/batches (harmony-integrated), where blood tissue typically harbors a moderate number of major immune lineages (T, B, NK, monocyte, DC) plus finer functional subsets and states within them. The 50-PC embedding used for clustering explains only ~25% of variance, so signal is somewhat diffuse across many components. Judge how finely to partition this embedding given the cell count and the expected number of genuine immune subpopulations versus the risk of splitting a single lineage into artefactual clusters.

framing.model: This is a blood subset (tissue_general == blood) with 8305 cells organized into 14 Leiden clusters (resolution 0.8) across 25 batches, harmony-integrated. The matrix reports sctab_feature_space=true but has 15290 genes (not the standard 19331) and gene names were attached post-hoc from scTab's var.parquet since the export itself carried none, which is a risk for any method that depends on exact feature alignment. Blood is one of the best-annotated tissues for canonical immune marker vocabularies. Decide which annotation approach fits: a per-cluster marker-based method leveraging the 14 clusters and blood's well-known marker genes, a per-cell classifier using a curated blood/immune reference, or a per-cell de novo classifier that needs the matrix to truly sit in its fixed 19331-gene feature space.

criteria.markers_llm: Claude reads the top marker genes per cluster and names it. No reference model and no GPU; strongest when the tissue is well described in the literature and the clusters are clean.
criteria.celltypist: Logistic-regression classifier over curated references. Per-cell rather than per-cluster, CPU-cheap; strongest when a reference model matching this tissue exists.
criteria.jev_markers: Jev scores each cluster's marker genes against a fixed cell-type vocabulary and returns a calibrated probability per type. Per-cluster, sub-second, and the only option that can decline to answer when the markers are ambiguous.
